recommended_order.title: Sets and Functions
recommended_order.reason: Domain/codomain/range distinctions materially ease image and kernel work. Tutorial17592186173160 and example17592186171840 distinguish actual range from codomain; mastered IntroLinearT teaches arrow notation and linearity without this distinction. All49 questions are notation/range interpretation, not logarithmic domain computation.

recommended_order.title: Gaussian Elimination For NxM Systems of Equations
recommended_order.reason: The rectangular/free-variable extension is short enough to earn its place before null-space and 4x6 homework work. Studied RREF/singular 3x3 supply operations, but no direct learned rectangular lesson exists.

recommended_order.title: Subspaces of N-Dimensional Space
recommended_order.reason: First actual subspace criterion lesson; symbolic arbitrary-vector closure examples have real instructional value before image proofs. Entire practice is line/plane classification, so proof production remains a separate transfer demand.

recommended_order.title: Subspaces of N-Dimensional Space: Geometric Interpretation
recommended_order.reason: Outside expansion, but earns a place as a concrete sequel: bounded and nonlinear sets containing zero defeat the misleading origin-only heuristic from line/plane examples.

recommended_order.title: Calculating the Dot Product Using Angle and Magnitude
recommended_order.availability_reason: Lesson needs at least five fresh, gradable questions per skill: Calculating the Dot Product of Two Vectors Given Their Magnitudes and Angle has 0 (needs 5 more); Calculating the Dot Product of Two Vectors Given Their Magnitudes and Directions has 0 (needs 5 more); Calculating Dot Product Expressions Using the Properties of the Dot Product has 0 (needs 5 more)
recommended_order.reason: Despite its geometry title, this 13-question whole lesson explicitly teaches distributivity/scalar linearity, the exact algebra used in WHW5 4.10.44. Retain this modest whole lesson to make the proof algebra explicit; learned nD Vectors practices component products, while this lesson directly practices distributivity. Graph has prior repetitions 2 but no learned flag.

recommended_order.title: The Column Space of a Matrix
recommended_order.reason: Keep the concrete membership/consistency foundation even though Image/Rank repeats the definition later. Learner has no learned column-space lesson; this stages a new set concept before basis extraction/rank/image vocabulary.

recommended_order.title: The Null Space of a Matrix
recommended_order.reason: Keep elementary zero-product membership and parametric null-set work before extracting a basis. Matrix-vector product is mastered; the null-set interpretation is unstudied and has only one recorded practice mass.

recommended_order.title: Finding a Basis of a Span
recommended_order.reason: Foundational basis lesson is needed despite learned independence: distinguishes independent spanning subset from redundant generating set and explains why deletion preserves span.

recommended_order.title: Finding a Basis of the Column Space of a Matrix
recommended_order.reason: Although Basis of a Span has the algorithm, retain matrix-specific practice and original-column warning: WHW-5 #8 requires the column-space basis alongside a different row-basis rule. No mastered basis-extraction topic supplies this distinction.

recommended_order.title: The Dimension of a Span
recommended_order.reason: Basis size as dimension is new; includes ambient dim(R^n)=n needed for cardinality proofs, not merely numerical rank.

recommended_order.title: Expressing the Coordinates of a Vector in a Given Basis
recommended_order.reason: Coordinates for an arbitrary ordered basis are not supplied by mastered standard-matrix computation. Concrete forward/reverse representation practice substantially eases applying T to an expansion in an arbitrary basis.

recommended_order.title: The Rank of a Matrix
recommended_order.reason: Links dimension/column basis to pivots and nonzero echelon rows. No learned rank record exists, so do not replace conceptual rank learning with mastered pivot counting.

recommended_order.title: Finding a Basis of the Null Space of a Matrix
recommended_order.reason: Outside expansion and necessary for efficient whole-lesson nullity/IMT learning: turns free-variable descriptions into independent generators, including empty basis of zero space.

recommended_order.title: The Dimension of the Null Space of a Matrix
recommended_order.reason: Outside expansion but supplies the genuinely new correspondence free variables <-> null basis size before IMT asks students to interpret parametric null spaces.

recommended_order.title: Finding Determinants Using Laplace Expansions
recommended_order.reason: Keep non-first-row and column expansion because full retained lessons require this method, even though first-row expansion/elimination could compute the same number.

recommended_order.title: Basic Properties of Determinants
recommended_order.reason: Supplies triangular/identity/transpose determinant properties and meaningful practice; whole lesson also teaches determinant-volume interpretation that must remain in readiness analysis.

recommended_order.title: Row and Column Operations on Determinants
recommended_order.reason: Teaches effects of swapping, row scaling, replacement, whole-matrix scaling, and corresponding column operations, with dedicated concept practice.

recommended_order.title: Finding Determinants Using Row and Column Operations
recommended_order.reason: Actual4x4 reduction practice is needed for whole WHW 4; retain row AND column variants because this is a whole lesson.

recommended_order.title: Conditions When a Determinant Equals Zero
recommended_order.reason: Retain basic zero-determinant conceptual practice before full Further Properties; this is not optional merely because its facts can be rederived during downstream exercises.

recommended_order.title: Further Properties of Determinants
recommended_order.reason: Multiplicativity, inverse determinant, and row/column linearity directly support required homework proofs. Computing det(A^-1) does not require computing A^-1.

recommended_order.title: The Invertible Matrix Theorem in Terms of 2x2 Systems of Equations
recommended_order.reason: Keep a concrete first statement of inverse/determinant/unique-solution equivalence before its higher-dimensional vector-space reformulation. Entire questions are theorem implications, so inverse-matrix solving lesson is not required beforehand.

recommended_order.title: The Invertible Matrix Theorem in Terms of Dimension, Rank and Nullity
recommended_order.reason: New finite-dimensional equivalences explicitly explain why nullity zero forces all columns pivotal and Col(A)=R^n. This eases WHW-5 independent n vectors -> full span rather than leaving a theorem-transfer leap.

recommended_order.title: The Rank-Nullity Theorem
recommended_order.reason: Outside expansion, compact and explicitly covers matrix rank-nullity (confirmed textbook 4.10.5); rank and nullity separately do not themselves give the integrated theorem practice.

recommended_order.title: The Image and Rank of a Linear Transformation
recommended_order.reason: Actual image membership, standard-matrix bridge and rank(T)=dim im(T) need a complete lesson. It does not prove image closure or the arbitrary-basis image equality.

recommended_order.title: The Kernel of a Linear Transformation
recommended_order.reason: Outside expansion; first kernel vocabulary, basis and nullity of a transformation. Parent verified textbook5.7 explicitly requires kernels, kernel bases and trivial-kernel criterion.

recommended_order.title: The Invertible Matrix Theorem in Terms of Linear Transformations
recommended_order.reason: Textbook5.3 inverse-map equivalence and5.7 trivial-kernel criterion; whole practice explicitly connects collisions T(v1)=T(v2) to a nonzero kernel vector (17592186125118/17592186272020). This also supplies bijection/invertibility language assumed in transformation rank-nullity. Parent and subspace auditor independently agreed to retain.

recommended_order.title: The Rank-Nullity Theorem in Terms of Linear Transformations
recommended_order.reason: Outside expansion; parent verified textbook5.7 explicitly requires dimension(V)=dimension(kernel)+dimension(image). Descriptions of image/kernel and bijection implications make transfer from the matrix theorem substantially easier.

recommended_order.title: Dilations and Reflections as Linear Transformations
recommended_order.reason: Textbook 5.4 requires axes reflections and rotation/reflection compositions; this is the closest captured whole lesson for reflection matrices. Its dilation skill adds overhead but the reflection tutorial and skill are substantive, unlearned, and absent from learned Standard Matrix.

recommended_order.title: Rotations as Linear Transformations
recommended_order.reason: Textbook 5.4 explicitly requires general rotation matrices and action on vectors; learned Standard Matrix only reads coefficients and does not teach the geometric matrix. This is an omitted root worth adding to the proposed sequence.

recommended_order.title: Shear and Stretch as Linear Transformations
recommended_order.reason: Retain as instructional preparation for the retained whole Combining Linear Transformations Using 2x2 Matrices (17592186050646): parent inspected its full bank and found assumed shear/stretch matrices in questions17592186092830,17592186281513,17592186092525,17592186092860. This is a real downstream requirement even though textbook5.4 itself has only rotations/reflections.

recommended_order.title: Combining Linear Transformations Using 2x2 Matrices
recommended_order.reason: Textbook5.3 and5.4 require composition and correct matrix order. Tutorials17592186093492/493 explain rightmost-first; examples17592186091940/941/942 scaffold objects and two/three matrices. All three practice skills inspected. Its shear/stretch questions justify adding the whole Shear/Stretch prerequisite.

recommended_order.title: Inverting Linear Transformations
recommended_order.reason: Textbook5.3 requires recovering preimages/inverse transformations. Tutorial17592186093436 derives v=T^-1 w; examples17592186092070/071 cover vector and polygon inversion. Already learned2x2 inverses and matrix products provide the computation; retained GeneralRotations teaches vertex packing before this lesson, so a separate Objects lesson adds little.
